content:
Guiding Claude (Opus 5.5), a Lean4 proof that characterizes the solvability of two vertex disjoint paths that visit every cell in a rectangle, also known as the two colour Zig-Zag Numberlink problem, or two colour "Flow Free" problem. Solvability is done through a finite check of pattern classes and can be done in linear time. If a solution exists, one can be constructed in polynomial time.

As far as I know, this was an open problem posed by Adcock et al. (10.48550) that is now resolved, at least for the two path case.

I've posted example code, a draft paper, description and the Lean4 code in a GitHub repository (R2K2ZZN) with the Lean proof located in the lean/ directory. The proof compiles with three axioms, propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, along with 154 native_decide axioms. The 154 native_decide axioms were used due to speed concerns, with compile time being orders of magnitude faster using native_decide.

I have tried to do my due diligence to make sure the problem statement has been transferred over faithfully but if anyone finds flaws or other issues, I would welcome the feedback. I would also welcome any other constructive criticism about the project or proof.
